newsitem.title: USA: GM sets U.S. Buick Regal price at $20,545.
newsitem.headline: GM sets U.S. Buick Regal price at $20,545.

text.p: General Motors Corp said Wednesday the U.S. price for its all-new 1997-1/2 Buick Regal LS sedan will start at $20,545, about $800 higher than the 1996 model it replaces.
GM's Buick Motor Division said the new Regal LS features additional standard features valued at $1,200.
The Regal GS, powered by a super-charged version of the 3.8-liter V-6 engine in the LS model, will start at $22,945, about $1,200 higher than the 1996 Regal Gran Sport.
New standard equipment on th 1997-1/2 Regal GS is valued at $2,300, Buick said.
The additional equipment on both cars includes remote keyless entry, traction control, four-wheel anti-lock disc brakes, leather-wrapped steering wheel and an air filtration system.
Regal brand manager Roger Adams said the Regal is priced less than most comparably equipped competitors, including Ford Motor Co's Mercury Sable LS and Honda Motor Co Ltd's Honda Accord LX.
Regal GS will be over $2,000 less than the V-6 Toyota Motor Corp Camry XLE.

Buick is trying to position the new Regal as a high-value sport sedan. "The differences between Regal and domestic and import competition are striking," Adams said. "They underscore the built-in value Regal represents."
Both the Regal LS and GS will be available at dealerships this spring.
